parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: A sinusoidal alternating voltage has a root-mean-square (r.m.s.) potential difference (p.d.) of $4.2\text{V}$ and a frequency of $50\text{kHz}$.
parts.text:
The alternating voltage is applied across a resistor of resistance $760\Omega$.

By considering the peak voltage, show that the maximum power dissipated by the resistor is $46\text{mW}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 7.1, draw a smooth curve to show how the power $P$ dissipated in the resistor varies with time $t$ between $t = 0$ and $t = 40\mu\text{s}$. Assume that $P = 0$ when $t = 0$.
{{figure:9702_w22_43_q07_figure_7_1}}

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Use your line in (a)(ii) to explain why the mean power dissipated in the resistor is $23\text{mW}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: The alternating voltage in (a) is now applied to a piezoelectric crystal in air.
parts.text: Explain what happens to the air surrounding the crystal.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
A second piezoelectric crystal is placed in the air near to the first crystal.

Explain the effect of the surrounding air in (b)(i) on the second crystal.
